newsitem.title: CANADA: APEC officials tackle sectoral free trade.
newsitem.headline: APEC officials tackle sectoral free trade.

text.p: Senior trade officials from the Asia-Pacific region began a three-day meeting in Quebec City on Tuesday to decide which sectors to consider in establishing free trade in the region, a Canadian official said.
"I hope that after three days we'll have in place a process to isolate sectors," Len Edwards, a senior Canadian trade official who is chairing the meeting, told Reuters by telephone from Quebec City.

Canada is hosting this year's meetings of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation forum. Trade ministers from the group's 18 countries met in Montreal last weekend to prepare for a summit meeting in Vancouver in November.
APEC aims to foster free trade among its member developed countries by 2010 and among the developed and developing countries by 2020.
The officials this week hope to work on 15 suggestions for sectoral liberalisation that arose from the trade ministers' meeting, Edwards said.
"Each economy will have to develop their proposals in a great deal of detail," he said.
By August, the officials should have a solid idea what sectors are the most ideal for regional free trade. Their suggestions will shape the agenda for the Vancouver summit.

APEC members have suggested isolating trade in environmental products, chemicals, petrochemicals, steel, non-ferrous metals, pulp, paper, wood products and a few other sectors as possibilities for sectoral liberalisation, Edwards said.
The United States backed an expansion through APEC of an agreement to free up trade in information technology, he said.
The countries also committed to promoting free trade in financial services through a process set up by the World Trade Organisation.
The senior officials would also use this week's meetings to package initiatives on sustainable development as well as infrastructure funding and development in the Asia-Pacific region, Edwards said.
